title: Lumen Tutors: how to double regular students
prompt: Lumen is a US online marketplace where students book lessons with independent tutors. Growth has slowed while marketing costs keep rising. The CEO wants to double the number of new regular students Lumen gains each quarter within 12 months. How would you approach this?

facts.answer: Students book one-to-one online lessons with independent tutors. The average lesson costs $40 and Lumen keeps a 25% commission.
A regular student is one who has booked at least three lessons. Regular students are Lumen's profitable customers.
Double the number of new regular students gained per quarter, from 800 to 1,600, within 12 months.
A regular student books about 4 lessons a month and stays for about 10 months on average.
Lumen spent $240,000 on marketing last quarter, mostly on search and social ads. Competitors are bidding up the price of search ads.
Visitors to the site can sign up, then book a first lesson, then become regular students. The funnel data is available.
Tutor supply is not a constraint: about 20% of tutors' available hours are currently unbooked.
Marketing spend and new regular students have both risen over the last four quarters. The data by quarter is available.
Several competitors spend heavily on search ads. Lumen's tutors are well rated and its prices are in line with the market.
Lumen has no plans to change its commission or enter new countries this year. The CEO is open to product changes.

key_buckets: Where the funnel loses people: visit, sign-up, first lesson, regular
Acquisition: cost per regular student and channel efficiency
Retention and value: lessons per month and months retained
Levers by effort and impact: conversion, retention, new channels
good_signs: Maps the funnel and quantifies each stage
Recognises that rising spend is buying fewer students per dollar
Compares customer lifetime value with acquisition cost
Prioritises levers by impact and effort and proposes tests
red_flags: Recommends only 'spend twice as much on ads'
Looks only at the biggest percentage drop-off without considering what is easiest to improve
Lists ideas with no numbers or prioritisation

exhibits.title: Last quarter's funnel
exhibits.reveal_hint: Ask for the funnel from website visits to regular students, with conversion at each stage.
exhibits.insight: Only 0.8% of visitors become regular students. The biggest percentage loss is at sign-up (92% of visitors do not sign up), but every stage multiplies: a 25% relative improvement at any one stage lifts regular students by 25%.

exhibits.title: Marketing spend and new regular students by quarter
exhibits.reveal_hint: Ask how marketing spend and new regular students have changed over the last four quarters.
exhibits.insight: Spend rose 50% (from $160k to $240k) but new regular students rose only 25% (from 640 to 800). Cost per new regular student rose from $250 to $300.

math.question: What was the marketing cost per new regular student in Q4, in dollars?
How much commission does Lumen earn from one regular student over their lifetime, in dollars?
math.working: 4 lessons x $40 x 25% = $40 a month. Over 10 months that is $400.

math.question: What is the ratio of lifetime commission to acquisition cost?
math.working: $400 / $300 is about 1.3. Each dollar of marketing returns about $1.30 of commission over a student's life, which leaves little margin once other costs are covered.

math.question: If the first-lesson booking rate rose from 40% to 50% and nothing else changed, how many new regular students would Lumen gain per quarter?
math.working: 100,000 visits x 8% = 8,000 sign-ups; x 50% = 4,000 first lessons; x 25% = 1,000 regular students. That is a 25% gain on 800.

brainstorm.question: What could Lumen do to turn more visitors into regular students without relying only on more advertising?
idea_bank: Improve landing pages and sign-up flow to lift the visitor-to-sign-up rate
Offer a discounted or free trial first lesson to raise first-lesson bookings
Match new students to a suitable tutor faster, with recommendations
Sell lesson packages so students commit to several lessons upfront
Send reminders and follow-up emails to students who signed up but have not booked
Launch a referral scheme that rewards students and tutors
Partner with schools, parent groups or universities for lower-cost acquisition
Ask tutors to bring their own students onto the platform
Create content such as study guides to earn free search traffic

must_mention: Acquisition is getting more expensive: cost per new regular student rose from $250 to $300
Funnel stages multiply, so doubling needs improvements at several stages (for example, about +25% at three stages gives roughly 2x)
Lifetime commission is only about 1.3x acquisition cost, so improving conversion and retention beats buying more traffic
good_signs: Prioritises levers by impact and effort
Sets a target for each funnel stage and a plan to test
Names the metrics to track each quarter

model_answer_outline: Clarify the goal: new regular students per quarter from 800 to 1,600 within 12 months; confirm the definition of regular and that tutor supply is not a constraint.
Structure: funnel conversion, acquisition cost, retention and value, levers by effort and impact, targets and tests.
Funnel: 100,000 visits, 8% sign up, 40% book a first lesson, 25% become regular, giving 800. Each stage multiplies.
Economics: spend rose 50% but regular students only 25%, so cost per regular student rose from $250 to $300. Lifetime commission is $400, only 1.3x acquisition cost.
Maths on levers: lifting the first-lesson rate from 40% to 50% adds 25% (to 1,000 students). Roughly +25% at three separate stages is about 1.95x, close to double.

Recommendation: stop scaling paid ads, then run three tests: a better sign-up flow, a discounted first lesson plus faster tutor matching, and lesson packages to lift the rate of becoming regular. Add a referral scheme. Review results each quarter and reinvest in ads only when cost per regular student falls.
